Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • On every signed-in product screen wider than a phone, as the left column of ds-split.
  • To name the product's top-level places (up to six), a few saved or secondary places under a short heading, and the person who is signed in.
  • With a back row at the top ("All workspaces") when the product sits inside a larger container the person can leave.

When not to use

  • On public pages: use cmp-site-header.
  • For the path to the current page or for page actions: use cmp-page-header.
  • For steps through a flow: use cmp-step-list.
  • On phone-width product screens: show only cmp-page-header with an up link (see fdn-navigation).
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

Not applicable: one look. Density and Radius settings change its spacing and corners; the structure never changes.

Anatomy

Built from:

  • cmp-list-row, variant compact — every destination and the back row: icon in ds-list-row__leading, label in ds-list-row__text, an optional count in ds-list-row__trailing. The current destination carries aria-current="page".
  • cmp-avatar, variant sm — the signed-in person in the footer, with aria-hidden="true" because the name is written beside it. In a screen it shows the signed-in persona's portrait over the initials, as cmp-avatar describes.
  • cmp-icon-button, variant quiet — one action for the signed-in person (settings or sign out).

Own parts:

  • Root: <nav class="ds-sidebar-nav" aria-label="Main">, 232 px wide (the layout sidebar width) and as tall as its column.
  • ds-sidebar-nav__brand: an <a> (to the product's home) or <div> holding ds-sidebar-nav__mark (one letter or a ds-icon, on the ink fill) and ds-sidebar-nav__name (the product name, with an optional ds-sidebar-nav__sub line such as the workspace).
  • ds-sidebar-nav__group: a <div> of rows. The first group may hold only the back row; the main group holds the primary destinations.
  • ds-sidebar-nav__heading: a <p> naming a secondary group ("Saved", "For agents").
  • ds-sidebar-nav__footer: pinned to the bottom, holding the avatar, ds-sidebar-nav__person (name, with ds-sidebar-nav__role below) and the icon button.

Accessibility

  • The root is a nav landmark with an aria-label ("Main"), distinct from any other nav on the screen.
  • Each destination is a link; the current one has aria-current="page", and its raised highlight and strong weight mark it without relying on colour.
  • Icons in rows are decorative; the label is the accessible name. Counts are read after the label ("Activity 12"); add ds-visually-hidden words ("12 new") when the number alone would be unclear.
  • The footer's icon button has an aria-label that names its action.
  • Reading and Tab order follow the visual order: brand, back row, primary destinations, secondary groups, footer.

Interaction

  • Rows answer hover and press with a colour change within the quick duration; nothing moves or resizes (int-01, int-03).
  • Focus is always visible on every row and on the footer button, and opening a destination never leaves focus behind on a hidden element (int-02).
  • Changing the current destination swaps the highlight instantly; the sidebar itself never animates (int-04, int-06).

Content rules

  • Destination labels are one or two nouns people use, in sentence case: "Activity", "Saved views". The same order on every screen.
  • Counts appear only when they help people decide where to go next, and never above 999 ("999+").
  • Group headings are one or two words. At most two secondary groups.
  • The brand shows the product name; the sub line names where the person is (a workspace or team), not a slogan.

Do and don't

  • Do keep exactly one row marked current, matching the page the main column shows.
  • Do put the back row first when the product lives inside something larger, and keep it out of the main group.
  • Don't nest a second sidebar or put tabs inside it.
  • Don't hide primary destinations behind a menu on a desktop screen.
  • Don't restyle the rows here; if a destination needs a different look, add a declared variant to cmp-list-row first.
